correctness.rationale: For vertex in color a, the neighbor count of a is c_a-1 and of b!=a is c_b. This yields exactly three cases by number of globally most-populated colors: unique winner implies one-update unanimity; exactly two maxima exchange forever; three or more maxima are fixed. A coefficient extraction with exactly two maximum bins counts states, whose cycle count is half. Exact multinomial factorial moments produce Poisson(lambda) size-k cells under q~c*n^(k/(k-1)); higher-size bins vanish by union bound and (k-1)-cell counts diverge by second moments, proving the limit lambda^2 exp(-lambda)/2. The same moment argument proves disappearance between critical exponents. Embedded exhaustive checker confirmed all q=2..5 and n=2..8 (585996 states), independent of the coefficient recurrence in its direct graph transitions. Limits: fixed k only, n>=2 and q>=2.

value.rationale: The rule is a natural deterministic full-neighborhood plurality process and the exact orbit criterion captures the central distinction between unique plurality and nonconvergence. Beyond the known birthday case k=2, every fixed k>=3 has a separate critical palette power n^(k/(k-1)), and all those peaks share the exact maximum 2 exp(-2). The sharp exact coefficient count and multiscale stochastic nonconvergence benchmark are useful for studying how growing opinion diversity affects network stabilization. This is not presented as a mere special case of binary majority or as a new general Poisson theorem.
